submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE was 0.01665% at index 3 (Pb 0.74). Index 0 (Pb 0.83) gave 0.01572% and index 14 (Pb 0.49) gave 0.00282%. The Pb-rich films probably contain a Pb3O4 + Pb2Sb2O7 mixture that absorbs 2.4 eV light. Pb3O4 is on the MACE hull with a predicted gap of about 0.95 eV. Pb2Sb2O7 alone has a predicted gap of about 2.5 eV, close to the photon energy.

rejected.reason: Close to single-phase Pb2Sb2O7. Its predicted gap (~2.5 eV) is at or above the 2.4 eV photon energy, and its measured EQE was about 6x lower.
Not measured because the budget ran out. Its predicted gap of 2.69 eV is above the photon energy, so it should absorb poorly.

consultations.verdict: Support: Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore (Pb:Sb=1:1) is on the MACE hull with HSE-level gap ~2.5 eV, close to the 2.4 eV illumination; PbSb2O6 gap 2.69 eV absorbs less. Index 14 (Pb 0.489) is closest to single-phase Pb2Sb2O7.
Support: Pb3O4 predicted gap 0.95 eV (strong absorption at 2.4 eV); the pyrochlore at 1:1 gave very low EQE, so probe the Pb-rich end where Pb-oxide/Pb-rich mixed phases absorb 2.4 eV photons.

Moderate support: Pb3O4 is on the hull, so Pb-rich films likely hold a Pb3O4 + Pb2Sb2O7 mixture that absorbs 2.4 eV light. Index 0 beat index 14 by 5x. Index 3 (Pb 0.74) tests whether the optimum is a mixed-phase composition inside the Pb-rich region; the GP UCB also picks it.
